about.title: San Carlos Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a crash on El Camino Real, US-101, San Carlos Avenue, or Holly Street changes everything, and it's common for surviving spouses, domestic partners, and children to feel unsure of what comes next. California law allows certain close family members, and in some cases other dependents, to bring a wrongful death claim, but the window to act is limited to two years from the date of death, and even shorter if a government entity is involved. San Carlos sees dozens of injury collisions each year, most heavily on Friday evenings, and while San Carlos Avenue's 2025 numbers show no traffic deaths, families elsewhere in San Mateo County still face this loss regularly. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge a fee; we simply connect families with an independent attorney who can review what happened, explain available options, and help pursue accountability while the family focuses on grieving and healing.

whyChoose.title: Why San Carlos Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Standing Rules Are Specific
items.desc: California limits who may file a wrongful death claim, generally spouses, domestic partners, and children first, then other dependents or heirs. An attorney can clarify where your family fits before any deadline passes.

items.title: The Clock Starts at Death
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, and that window shrinks significantly if a government agency or public roadway maintenance is involved. Acting sooner preserves evidence and options.

items.title: No Upfront Cost to Get Answers
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover compensation for your family. LawProactive's connection service itself is always free.

items.question: Who in our family is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: California generally gives first priority to a surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, and children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may qualify. An attorney can review your specific family situation and confirm who has standing.

items.question: Is a wrongful death claim the same as a criminal case against the driver?
items.answer: No, they're separate. A criminal case is brought by the state and focused on punishment, while a wrongful death claim is a private civil action seeking compensation for the family's losses. Both can proceed independently of each other.

items.question: San Carlos Avenue and Holly Street see a lot of traffic — does that affect our claim?
items.answer: Higher collision counts on corridors like San Carlos Avenue, El Camino Real, and Holly Street don't change the legal standard for a wrongful death claim, but they can matter for gathering evidence, such as traffic camera footage or witness reports common to busy roads. An attorney can help identify what's available for your specific case.
